name: ETP Kafka
description: ETP infrastructure capability for Apache Kafka 3.8.1 event streaming. Documents producer and consumer client connectivity, topic infrastructure conventions, and deployment targets. Not a runtime ETP service or Kafka proxy.

version.description: Initial infrastructure capability documenting Kafka 3.8.1 KRaft local Docker, direct producer/consumer connectivity, and environment-specific deployment targets. Excludes REST APIs, Schema Registry, automatic provisioning, and UAM event implementation.

functional.summary: Apache Kafka 3.8.1 event streaming infrastructure for ETP applications. Supports producer and consumer connectivity. Not a JVM runtime service, REST API, or Kafka proxy.

producer.flow: Application → Kafka Producer Client → Kafka Broker → Topic → Partition
producer.description: Applications publish events directly via Kafka client libraries

consumer.flow: Kafka Broker → Topic → Partition → Consumer Group → Kafka Consumer Client → Application
consumer.description: Applications consume events directly via Kafka client libraries

provides: Apache Kafka 3.8.1 broker (Docker image apache/kafka:3.8.1, KRaft mode, no Zookeeper)
Kafka wire protocol for producer and consumer client libraries
Topic, partition, replication, and retention infrastructure (deployment-configured)
Configuration and operational conventions for environment-resolved bootstrap servers and secrets
doesNotProvide: ETP REST APIs for producing or consuming messages
Application topic names, consumer groups, or event semantics (consumer-owned)
Event processing, business rules, or payload validation logic
Confluent Schema Registry or Avro enforcement (future optional integration)
Connection brokering or message proxy in the ETP runtime path
applicationResponsibilities: Topic purpose and business event naming
Producer vs consumer role per flow
Event payload, schema reference, and business semantics
Serialization choice (e.g. String, JSON bytes) and deserializers
Offset strategy, acknowledgement mode, and business retry/error handling
Event processing, transformations, and JSON Schema validation (separate validation capability at application layer)
infrastructureResponsibilities: Network reachability from producer and consumer applications
Topic creation, partitions, replication factor, and retention (operator or deployment tooling)

kafkaCapability: Infrastructure support for topic creation and broker-level topic configuration
Default partition count and replication factor conventions for local dev
Retention and log directory persistence policy
application: Business topic names and event types
Producer and consumer binding to specific topics
Event payload structure and processing logic

clients: spring-kafka (Spring Boot spring-kafka with KafkaTemplate and @KafkaListener)
kafka.integration: Applications configure spring.kafka.* (or native client properties) and connect directly — no ETP Kafka middleware

producer.flow: Application → Kafka Producer Client → Kafka Broker → Topic → Partition

consumer.flow: Kafka Broker → Topic → Partition → Consumer Group → Kafka Consumer Client → Application

schemaRegistry.detail: No Schema Registry in repository. Kafka transports message bytes; application/event processing performs payload validation (e.g. JSON Schema Validation capability at application layer). Confluent Schema Registry is a future optional integration.

documentation.note: Infrastructure capability — no OpenAPI service surface

credentials: SASL username/password or other Kafka auth credentials via environment variables or secret manager
Never store live credentials in the Capability Registry contract document or registration payload
secretReferences: Production: secret manager / platform secret injection (deployment-specific)

authentication.localDevelopment: PLAINTEXT only in capabilities/kafka/docker-compose.yml — no SASL in local defaults
authentication.sasl: Supported by Kafka client libraries; not configured in repository local compose — deployment responsibility for non-dev

tlsSsl.detail: Local compose uses PLAINTEXT listeners. TLS is a deployment responsibility for managed Kafka (MSK, Azure Event Hubs for Kafka, etc.) in non-dev environments.

acls.detail: Kafka ACLs supported by broker; not configured in local v1.0.0 compose

networkAccess: Local development: Kafka port published via Docker Compose (default host port 59092)
Non-dev: restrict broker ports to application network; not configured in repository defaults
applicationIsolation: Topic and consumer group naming per application/service
Optional dedicated Kafka cluster per environment (deployment-specific)
ACL-based isolation in managed deployments (future hardening)
limitations: Single-node KRaft broker in local compose (replication factor 1)
No TLS or SASL in local Docker defaults
No ACL users in repository compose
futureHardening: SASL (SCRAM, OAuthBearer) for all non-dev environments
TLS/mTLS for broker and client connections
Kafka ACLs with least-privilege per producer/consumer

deployment.versionRationale: Apache Kafka 3.8.1 is the current stable 3.8 line with official Docker images, KRaft single-node simplicity for local dev, and broad spring-kafka compatibility. No prior Kafka version existed in the ETP repository.
deployment.implementationModel: Infrastructure broker container — not an ETP Spring Boot artifact
environmentSpecific: Docker Compose (local development — implemented in capabilities/kafka/)
Kubernetes Strimzi or Helm Kafka chart (deployment-specific — not defined in repository)
AWS MSK (deployment target — not implemented in repository)
Azure Event Hubs for Kafka / Azure-managed Kafka-compatible services (deployment target — not implemented in repository)
deployment.topicManagement: Operator or kafka-topics CLI; auto-create enabled in local compose for dev convenience

nfr.connectionReliability: Producer retries and acks configured per application; consumers define poll/retry and error-handling policy
nfr.healthReadiness: Container health via kafka-broker-api-versions; consumer application readiness via Kafka connectivity check (e.g. Spring Boot Actuator kafka health when configured)
nfr.messageDelivery: At-least-once by default; exactly-once requires idempotent producer and transactional settings at application/deployment layer
operationalRequirements: Start Kafka before consumers/producers that require connectivity at startup
Single-node local broker is not HA — deployment-specific clustering for production
No numeric latency or availability SLOs defined in repository for v1.0.0

startup: Create topics with appropriate partitions and replication (or rely on auto-create in dev only)
Start producer/consumer applications with Kafka client configuration
readiness: Kafka: kafka-broker-api-versions healthcheck in local Docker Compose
Applications: KafkaTemplate/@KafkaListener health or native client metadata request
operations.connectivity: Verified by application Kafka clients, not by a dedicated ETP Kafka service

offsets.owner: Kafka broker (__consumer_offsets internal topic) with consumer client offset commit policy
offsets.applicationPolicy: auto vs manual commit, auto.offset.reset — consumer configuration

migrations.note: Not applicable — Kafka has no Flyway equivalent at infrastructure layer; topic schema evolution is application-owned

operations.environmentConfiguration: Per-service environment variables (ETP_KAFKA_*) — see configuration section

clientConsumers: Any Kafka client compatible with Apache Kafka 3.x wire protocol
expectations: Producers and consumers use Kafka 3.x compatible client libraries
JSON payloads common; Avro/Protobuf without Schema Registry requires application-managed schema contracts

applicationCapabilityDependency.description: Composition-time: etp.kafka v1.0.0, required true/false — no plaintext secrets
applicationCapabilityDependency.example: capability: etp.kafka, version: 1.0.0, required: true for event-driven flows

applicationKafkaUsage.description: Producer/consumer role, logical event usage, topic reference, consumer group, serializers — application-owned

environmentConfiguration.description: Deployment-time: bootstrap servers, SASL, TLS, secret references — resolves Docker vs K8s vs MSK vs Azure

businessImplementation.description: Event handlers, producer logic, validation, business rules — not ETP Kafka capability configuration

parameters.name: key/value serializers
parameters.description: spring.kafka.producer.* / spring.kafka.consumer.* or native client properties

parameters.name: partitions / replication
parameters.description: Topic creation parameters — operator or deployment tooling, not application registry payload

dependencies.note: Kafka is infrastructure. Registry dependencies[] is empty. JSON Schema Validation and other processing capabilities are separate application-layer concerns, not registry dependencies of etp.kafka.
